newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor forms cellular phone bidding group.
newsitem.headline: Koor forms cellular phone bidding group.

text.p: Koor Industries said on Sunday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with three partners to bid for a license to operate a cellular telephone network in Israel.

The government published a tender last week for groups to bid for a third cellular operating license in competition with Pelephone, a joint venture of Bezeq Israel Telecom and the Israeli subsidiary of Motorola Inc, and Cellcom, whose shareholders include Bellsouth Corp.
The deadline for submitting proposals is August 28.

Koor said that under the terms of the memorandum, it would hold 28 percent of the bidding consortium. The other partners are Mannesmann Eurokom GmbH, a division of Germany's Mannesmann AG ; Southwestern Bell International Development Corp., a unit of SBC Communications Inc ; and Morris Kahn, a French investor who controls Israel's Aurec Group.
A Koor spokesman could not confirm the size of their holdings in the consortium. Koor said in a statement that other companies may still join.
"The signing of the memorandum is an additional step to realise the strategic plan which Koor has adopted regarding the expansion of its activities constituting its core business," Koor said.

Under the terms of the tender, consortia can be up to 80 percent foreign-controlled but at least 25 percent of the group must be controlled by a company already operating a cellular network outside of Israel.
The license will be for six years, with a 10-year renewal option.
